title: Wicked: For Good Opens Saturday — and Oz Is Poised to Break the Musical Box Office Record
excerpt: Wicked: For Good opens Saturday in theaters, with Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande returning to Oz and tracking pointing to a $112–155 million debut.
content:
Oz is back on the big screen. Wicked: For Good opens Saturday, November 21, in theaters, closing out the two-part adaptation of the Broadway musical — and the box office is already treating it like the biggest event of the fall.

The sequel picks up where last year’s Wicked left off, after Elphaba’s defiant flight in “Defying Gravity.” Elphaba, played by Cynthia Erivo, is now demonized as the Wicked Witch of the West, living in exile and fighting for the freedom of Oz’s silenced Animals while trying to expose the truth about the Wizard, played by Jeff Goldblum. Glinda, played by Ariana Grande, has become the glamorous public face of Goodness at the Emerald City palace — and the friendship at the heart of the story is being pulled in opposite directions.

Director Jon M. Chu returns for the second half, with Jonathan Bailey back as Fiyero and Michelle Yeoh as Madame Morrible. The film adapts the second act of the stage musical by Stephen Schwartz and Winnie Holzman, loosely based on Gregory Maguire’s 1995 novel. It runs 2 hours and 17 minutes and is rated PG.

What the first reviews say

Early reviews are mixed-to-positive, and the split is the story. The film sits at around 73% on Rotten Tomatoes in early reviews, below the first film’s 88%, while early audiences are far more enthusiastic, with the Popcornmeter around 97%. The one point nearly every critic agrees on is the performances: Erivo and Grande’s singing and chemistry carry the film.

How big could the opening be?

Deadline projects a domestic opening of $112 million to $115 million, with forecasts running as high as $155 million. Universal is projecting a more conservative $125 million domestically, with a global opening near $200 million. Advance ticket sales are running ahead of the first film’s pace. The first Wicked opened to $112.5 million domestically in the same pre-Thanksgiving window last year and went on to earn more than $756 million worldwide, with 10 Oscar nominations and two wins. The sequel reportedly cost about $150 million to make.

If the tracking holds, For Good would set the record for the biggest opening ever for a Broadway musical adaptation — beating the record set by the first film a year ago.

En México: Wicked: Por Siempre

The film opens the same day in Mexican theaters as Wicked: Por Siempre, in dubbed and subtitled versions. Cinépolis and Fundación Cinépolis are also bringing back “Funciones Relajadas” — relaxed screenings for neurodivergent audiences and people with sensory sensitivities — for the film on the weekends of November 28–29 and December 5–6 at nine Cinépolis complexes across Mexico, including Galerías Monterrey in Nuevo León.

What it means

Analysis: Universal split one stage musical into two films to avoid cutting plot points, and the gamble has already paid off once. The question now is whether the darker second half — a story about propaganda, friendship under pressure, and the road to Dorothy’s arrival in Oz — can match the first film’s warmth with audiences. The early numbers say the audience is already there. Whether the critics’ cooler reception matters at all will be answered at the box office this weekend.
